```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

```{r}
library(csvschema)
```

The wire format assumes a hostile channel: any CSV dialect, any locale, any
spreadsheet, any human with find-and-replace. `csvschema` ships a simulator for
every vector in its threat model --- the `cs_corrupt_*()` family --- so you can
apply a named corruption to a file and watch the reader recover from it, or
report exactly what broke.

```{r}
# A small fixture with values chosen to trip real spreadsheet coercions.
fixture <- data.frame(
  zip    = sprintf("%05d", c(1, 23, 456, 7890, 12345)),  # leading zeros
  bigid  = sprintf("1%015d", 1:5),                        # 16-digit strings
  region = factor(c("NE", "S", "MW", "W", "S")),
  note   = c("SEPT1", "Café", "normal", "0.5", "=SUM(A1)"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# Helpers: write the fixture, corrupt the file, read it back.
read_chr <- function(path) {
  read.csv(path, colClasses = "character", check.names = FALSE,
           na.strings = character(0))
}
write_chr <- function(df) {
  tmp <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv")
  utils::write.table(df, tmp, sep = ",", row.names = FALSE, na = "",
                     qmethod = "double", eol = "\n")
  tmp
}
```

## Two layers of protection

The schema packets are protected by a per-packet CRC and a whole-schema hash;
the **data** is protected by the `_canary` column, which stores a purposeful
sample of each variable's most fragile values plus a fingerprint of the whole
column. Recovery and canary results are independent: a file can lose rows (the
data changes, the schema survives) or be mangled by a spreadsheet (the schema
survives, the data is damaged).

## Row loss: schema survives, canary notices

Dropping rows at random leaves the striped, repeated schema intact:

```{r}
path <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv")
cs_write(fixture, path, verbose = FALSE)

thinned <- cs_corrupt_rows(read_chr(path), keep = 0.5, mode = "random", seed = 1)
out <- cs_read_csv(write_chr(thinned), sidecar = FALSE, verbose = FALSE)
cs_report(out)$status
```

## Spreadsheet coercion: schema survives, damage is named

`cs_corrupt_excel()` reproduces what a spreadsheet does on import: it strips
leading zeros, renders long digit strings in scientific notation, coerces
date-like strings to dates, and turns formula cells into `#NAME?`. The packets
(which begin with `{{`) match none of those rules, so the schema still verifies
--- but the canary check finds the damaged values and says *which kind* of
damage hit each variable.

```{r}
damaged <- cs_corrupt_excel(read_chr(path))
out <- suppressWarnings(cs_read_csv(write_chr(damaged), sidecar = FALSE,
                                    verbose = FALSE))
rep <- cs_report(out)
rep$status                                   # schema still verified
rep$canary[, c("variable", "verdict", "damage")]
```

Each damaged variable is mapped back to the detector that selected its lost
canary value, so `zip` reads "leading_zero", a coerced date reads "date_like",
and so on.

## Case folding: detected, not silently wrong

Some mainframe and SQL loaders upper- or lower-case every cell. That folds the
packet payloads too, and because each packet's CRC covers the exact-case
payload, the folded packets fail their check and are dropped. The reader does
**not** return a silently wrong schema --- it reports the loss:

```{r}
folded <- cs_corrupt_case(read_chr(path), mode = "upper")
out <- suppressWarnings(cs_read_csv(write_chr(folded), sidecar = FALSE,
                                    verbose = FALSE))
cs_report(out)$status                         # incomplete or absent, never verified
```

## The simulator family

```{r echo = FALSE}
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  Function = c("cs_corrupt_rows", "cs_corrupt_columns", "cs_corrupt_header",
               "cs_corrupt_excel", "cs_corrupt_encoding", "cs_corrupt_bom",
               "cs_corrupt_delimiter", "cs_corrupt_smartquotes",
               "cs_corrupt_whitespace", "cs_corrupt_truncate",
               "cs_corrupt_case", "cs_corrupt_merge", "cs_corrupt_eol",
               "cs_corrupt_replace", "cs_corrupt_invisible"),
  Vector = c("drop / reorder / duplicate rows",
             "drop columns; Text-to-Columns split",
             "remove or regenerate the header",
             "spreadsheet import coercions",
             "re-encode (mojibake), NFC/NFD",
             "prepend a UTF-8 BOM",
             "rewrite the delimiter",
             "straight quotes to curly, -- to em dash",
             "trim, pad, non-breaking spaces",
             "truncate every cell",
             "upper / lower / title case",
             "bind two different schemas",
             "CRLF / LF swap, drop trailing newline",
             "global find-and-replace",
             "insert zero-width and invisible characters")
), col.names = c("Function", "What it does"))
```

Each simulator records what it did in a `cs_corruption` attribute, so a
round-trip through several of them is self-documenting:

```{r}
x <- cs_corrupt_rows(read_chr(path), keep = 0.5, seed = 1)
attr(cs_corrupt_excel(x), "cs_corruption")
```
